findings.title: Missing essential trust pages: About Us, Contact, Privacy Policy
findings.why_it_matters: Clear institutional identity (About Us, Contact, Privacy Policy, Terms of Service) is a foundational trust requirement for both organic search ranking and AI knowledge graph verification.
findings.fix: Ensure dedicated About, Contact, Privacy Policy, and Terms pages are linked in your main navigation or footer.

findings.title: robots.txt Presence & Accessibility

evidence.error: robots.txt was not found or returned non-200 status code

findings.why_it_matters: robots.txt is the universal entry point for all web crawlers. Without it, crawlers may waste crawl budget on non-canonical URLs, internal search parameters, or private endpoints.
findings.fix: Publish a valid /robots.txt file at the root of your domain.

findings.title: Accidental Critical Path Blocking in robots.txt

evidence.message: No catastrophic global Disallow: / rule found.

findings.why_it_matters: Accidental 'Disallow: /' or disallowing core CSS/JS/images prevents search engines and AI crawlers from indexing content or rendering pages properly.
findings.fix: Audit Disallow rules in robots.txt to ensure the homepage ('/') and primary content paths remain accessible.

findings.title: XML Sitemap Discovery & Validity

evidence.error: No valid XML sitemaps discovered or sitemap was empty

findings.why_it_matters: XML sitemaps provide a roadmap of all canonical, high-value pages, ensuring search engines discover new and updated content rapidly.
findings.fix: Publish an XML sitemap at /sitemap.xml and reference it in /robots.txt.

findings.title: www vs. non-www Redirection Consistency
findings.why_it_matters: Allowing both www and non-www versions of a website to return 200 OK splits link authority and creates duplicate content across domains.
findings.fix: Configure web server or CDN (Cloudflare/Vercel) to redirect the non-canonical host with a 301 status.

findings.title: AI Bot & Crawler Access Matrix (Training vs. Search Bots)

evidence.message: All primary AI search bots are allowed access to the site.

findings.why_it_matters: AI vendors operate distinct web crawlers. Blocking training bots (GPTBot, ClaudeBot) protects copyright, but blocking search crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) destroys real-time citations and brand visibility in generative AI answers.
findings.fix: Configure robots.txt to explicitly permit AI search crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) while selectively enforcing policy for training bots based on your intellectual property strategy.

findings.title: CDN / WAF Bot Challenge or 403 Page Detection
findings.why_it_matters: Aggressive Cloudflare, CloudFront, or Akamai WAF rules often return JS challenge (CAPTCHA) pages or 403 Forbidden to non-browser requests, making content completely invisible to automated AI engines.
findings.fix: Configure CDN / Firewall rules to allow verified AI crawler IP ranges and user-agents without triggering managed browser challenges.

findings.title: No /llms.txt file detected (Optional modern AI standard)

evidence.note: Optional modern standard for AI agent context discovery.

findings.why_it_matters: The /llms.txt standard (proposed by Jeremy Howard and adopted by Anthropic, Perplexity, Cursor, etc.) provides AI agents and answer engines with a curated, token-efficient map of your site's core content and documentation in clean Markdown format.
findings.fix: Publish an /llms.txt file at your site root containing an H1 title, a concise blockquote summary, and markdown links to key documentation pages.

findings.title: Strong AI brand mention rate: 53.3% (95% CI: 30.1% - 75.2%, n=15)
findings.why_it_matters: Measures how frequently your brand name is recommended or cited across multiple queries in generative engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude). High mention rates indicate strong entity saliency.
findings.fix: Strengthen topical authority, earn citations in industry review publications (G2, Trustpilot, Forbes), and optimize passage structure so generative models associate your brand with high-intent solution queries.

findings.title: High AI citation rate: 40.0% (95% CI: 19.8% - 64.3%, n=15)
findings.why_it_matters: Live generative engines cite primary sources in web cards and footnotes. A high citation rate drives direct referral traffic from users exploring AI-synthesized responses.
findings.fix: Ensure robots.txt permits AI search crawlers, provide original statistics and data tables, and structure authoritative answer-first passages with clear citation anchors.

findings.title: Leading AI Share of Voice: 53.3%
findings.why_it_matters: Measures the proportion of queries where your brand is recognized versus competing products in the same niche.
findings.fix: Create high-value comparison pages and case studies addressing alternative solutions to capture conversational share.

findings.title: Identified 4 top cited third-party domains in AI answers
findings.why_it_matters: Identifies which third-party domains (e.g. Reddit, Wikipedia, G2, TechCrunch) AI engines prioritize when synthesizing recommendations for your category.
findings.fix: Prioritize digital PR and organic presence on the specific domains winning citations for your target queries.

findings.title: Thin content: Page contains only 193 words (<250 words)
findings.why_it_matters: Pages with less than 250 words offer little unique value to users, are flagged as low-quality under Google's Helpful Content guidelines, and are ignored by generative AI answer engines.
findings.fix: Expand thin pages with comprehensive answers, examples, or consolidate into parent category pages.

findings.title: Missing rel='canonical' Link Tag

evidence.error: No rel='canonical' tag found in page HTML

findings.why_it_matters: Without an explicit canonical tag, search engines must guess which version of a page to index, leading to duplicate content dilution across trailing slashes, HTTP/HTTPS, and query params.
findings.fix: Add a self-referencing <link rel='canonical' href='https://...'> tag in the <head>.

findings.title: Missing or Empty <title> Tag

evidence.error: Title tag is missing or whitespace only

findings.why_it_matters: The <title> tag is one of the most critical on-page ranking signals and provides the clickable headline in search engine results and AI answer cards.
findings.fix: Add a unique, descriptive <title> tag inside the <head> of every HTML page.

findings.title: Missing Meta Description
findings.why_it_matters: Meta descriptions provide the summary snippet in search results and help AI crawlers understand page intent before full parsing.
findings.fix: Add an enticing, descriptive <meta name='description' content='...'> tag.

findings.title: Missing <h1> heading tag

evidence.error: No <h1> heading tag found in page HTML

findings.why_it_matters: Every indexable page should have exactly one descriptive <h1> tag serving as the main topic header for users, search crawlers, and screen readers.
findings.fix: Ensure each page contains exactly one <h1> element accurately describing the page subject.

findings.title: Core Schema.org Type Coverage
findings.why_it_matters: No Schema.org entity types were detected on this page.
findings.fix: Deploy relevant Schema.org JSON-LD templates based on page intent.

findings.title: Time to First Byte (TTFB) Latency
findings.why_it_matters: High server response latency slows down crawling, burns crawl budget, degrades Core Web Vitals, and causes AI bots with short timeout thresholds (e.g. 800ms) to abort requests.
findings.fix: Optimize database queries, enable server-side caching, and utilize edge CDNs (Cloudflare/Fastly).

findings.title: Mobile Responsive Viewport Configuration

evidence.error: No valid viewport meta tag found

findings.why_it_matters: Mobile-first indexing requires a responsive viewport tag so pages render correctly across smartphones, tablets, and mobile crawlers.
findings.fix: Add <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0'> in the <head>.

findings.title: Missing recommended security headers (HSTS / nosniff)
findings.why_it_matters: Security headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options) protect visitors from clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and man-in-the-middle downgrade attacks.
findings.fix: Configure web server or CDN to send Strict-Transport-Security and X-Content-Type-Options headers.

findings.title: Moderate client-side text hydration: 37.5% of text rendered via JS
findings.why_it_matters: Many AI crawlers and indexing pipelines (e.g. GPTBot, PerplexityBot, Common Crawl) fetch raw HTML without running a full headless JavaScript browser. If key content requires client-side JavaScript to render, generative engines will completely miss that text.
findings.fix: Implement Server-Side Rendering (SSR), Static Site Generation (SSG), or Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) so that primary content is present in the initial HTTP response payload.

findings.title: 73 links require JavaScript to discover
findings.why_it_matters: AI and fast search crawlers that parse raw HTML will fail to discover these linked pages.
findings.fix: Ensure standard HTML `<a href>` elements are pre-rendered in the server HTML for all internal navigation and pagination links.

findings.title: Text Trapped in Canvas, Iframes, or Complex SVGs
findings.why_it_matters: Text rendered inside <canvas> elements or loaded inside third-party <iframe> embeds is completely invisible to standard text extractors used by LLM search agents.
findings.fix: Provide server-rendered HTML text transcripts, data tables, or accessible DOM text alternatives alongside canvas visualizations or iframes.

findings.title: Bot Response Latency (TTFB < 800ms for Real-Time AI Search)
findings.why_it_matters: Real-time AI search bots (Perplexity, ChatGPT web search) operate on tight sub-second budgets while streaming answers to users. Pages with Time To First Byte (TTFB) > 800ms are frequently skipped or timed out during live search synthesis.
findings.fix: Optimize edge CDN caching, enable HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, and optimize backend database queries so that bot requests respond with TTFB under 500ms.
